name: Ruddy Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southeastern venezuela and northern brazil (cerro uei-tepui in roraima)
description: A small, charismatic bird of tepui highland forests. Note orange-rufous face and breast, short tail, and bold wing bars.

name: Blue Crane
rangeDescription: Locally in northern namibia, southern zimbabwe and south africa
description: A small, elegant, uniformly blue-gray crane that dwells in open habitats in pairs and variably sized groups. The bulbous head, plain face lacking any naked skin, and lack of contrast in the wings are distinctive.

name: Scott's Oriole
rangeDescription: Arid southwestern usa to southern mexico
description: This black-and-yellow oriole prefers dry habitats where yuccas are plentiful, often on steep hillsides. Males are particularly striking; look for the black back, head, and breast, bright white wingbar, and yellow shoulder.

name: King Vulture
rangeDescription: Southern mexico to northern argentina and brazil
description: Uncommon, large, and spectacular bird of lowland tropical forest, mainly in wilder areas and not around human habitation. Most often seen soaring overhead in mid-late morning, often fairly high up with kettles of Black Vultures; rarely seen perched.

name: Yellow-rumped Siskin
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Fairly common locally in the Andes, often near bogs or other areas with water. Often in flocks, feeding on the ground or in low bushes.

name: Cameroon Indigobird
rangeDescription: Discontinuously distributed from sierra leone eastward to northeastern democratic republic of the congo and south sudan
description: A nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of African and Black-bellied Firefinches and Brown and Dybowski's Twinspots. Breeding males are glossy black with blue iridescence and a pale brownish panel in the wings.

name: Allen's Gallinule
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa, madagascar, and comoros
description: When seen in good light, shows spectacular purple-and-green coloration. In dull light, looks dark, but still shows red bill and feet, pale blue forehead shield, and white undertail.

name: Atiu Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Atiu (southern cook archipelago)
description: A small, mostly brownish swiftlet. Most obvious feature is a pale gray throat contrasting with a darker brownish belly.

name: Mongolian Finch
rangeDescription: Sparse montane vegetation of southwestern and central asia
description: A pale, large-billed finch found in dry areas with sparse plant cover. Usually seen in small and medium-sized groups.

name: Blue Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Society islands, cook islands, and western tuamotu archipelago
description: A unique and distinctive lorikeet, almost entirely a deep royal blue with a bright orange bill and feet and an extensive pure white throat, cheek, and chest patch. Inhabits any forest, but appears to favor coconut and banana plantations.

name: White-edged Oriole
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of western ecuador and northwestern peru (southward to la libertad)
description: Bright orange-and-black bird found in dry forest in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru. The only other oriole in its range is Yellow-tailed Oriole; White-edged lacks yellow on the underside of the tail, has more extensive white in the wing, and is usually (but not always) a deeper orange color.

name: Rufous Twistwing
rangeDescription: Southwestern amazonia in southeastern peru, southwestern brazil, and northwestern bolivia
description: Large flycatcher with uniform bright cinnamon plumage. Inhabits the understory of large stands of bamboo within humid forests.

name: Mangrove Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern australia (central queensland to hastings river, new south wales)
description: Medium-sized honeyeater found in coastal habitats of eastern Australia. Back is brown-green, breast is gray, and underparts are pale.

name: Gilbert's Whistler
rangeDescription: Southern western australia to northern victoria and southwestern and central new south wales
description: Chunky gray songbird with heavy black bill, found in dry forest and bushland across semi-arid southern Australia. Male has pale orange throat and dark, not orange, in lores (compare Red-lored Whistler).

name: Ticking Doradito
rangeDescription: Breeds central chile, and western argentina; winters northward to bolivia
description: Very local little bird of fresh and brackish marshes and adjacent weedy vegetation in lowlands. Departs Chile in the winter (mainly late March to mid-October) for unknown areas east of the Andes.

name: Gray-breasted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Interior southwestern mexico (northern guerrero and morelos to east-central oaxaca)
description: Fairly common endemic woodpecker in desert interior habitats of southwest Mexico, especially in areas with tall columnar cacti, including towns and villages. Often in pairs or small groups.

name: Short-billed Miner
rangeDescription: Breeds southern chile and southern argentina; winters northward to mendoza
description: Breeds in Tierra del Fuego and adjacent southern Patagonia; migrates north in winter. Favors open shrub steppe, grassy areas, and gravel roadsides.

name: Diamantina Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Chapada diamantina region of northeastern brazil (bahia)
description: Gray tapaculo with a black-barred buff vent. Females are browner above.

name: Abbott's Starling
rangeDescription: Mount kenya southward to mount meru and mount kilimanjaro
description: A small, distinctive starling with a tiny range in Kenya and Tanzania. The male has a blue-black back and breast and a white belly.

name: Stripe-cheeked Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands and foothills on both slopes of panama
description: This scarce small woodpecker is golden-olive above and barred below. The male has a red crown, a red mustache stripe, and a yellow stripe below the eye.
